⚡️ Tehran will not bow to Washington’s dictates, Foreign Ministry spokesperson says

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei has stressed that Tehran bases its decisions on national interests and will not bow to Washington’s dictates or attempts to impose its excessive demands.

Speaking at a weekly press conference on Tuesday, Baqaei offered condolences over the martyrdom of three Iranians in the US attack on Larak Island.
​
Asked about the ministry’s “approach and view regarding the current status of negotiations with the United States,” Baqaei said that the ministry assesses developments and expresses its views based on the country’s interests and national considerations, and ultimately will act in accordance with whatever is decided by the competent authorities.
​
Baqaei acknowledged that the US officials are confused in their approaches and statements, but said this would not cause Iran to neglect its own capabilities.
​
“We will use the tools of diplomacy wherever necessary to explain our positions and secure the rights of the Iranian nation,” he said.
​
Baqaei added that Pakistan and several other countries are continuing efforts to de-escalate tensions and end the war, while Pakistan’s military chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, visited Iran as part of Islamabad’s role as a friendly and neighboring country and presented his views. He stressed that Iran’s constant criterion is safeguarding its national interests.
​
The spokesperson said that the US attack was not something new for Iran, noting that Washington has repeatedly carried out acts of aggression under various pretexts and received the necessary response.
​
He further noted that these actions reflect US ill intent and confusion, stemming from its excessive demands and its mistaken belief that negotiations mean dictating terms—an approach that will not work with Iran. “We must remain fully vigilant against enemy moves, and any aggression will be met with a response,” he added.
​
Baqaei said that the US must be held accountable for its blatant violation of the Islamabad memorandum of understanding, adding that Iran will decide how to proceed based on circumstances. For now, he said, the focus is on defense and resistance against the US’s excessive demands.

🇷🇺 Beslan remembers: 22 years since the School No. 1 terrorist attack

More than 2,000 people paid their respects to the victims of the Beslan school terrorist attack on the first day of the three-day “Memorial Watch,” according to the North Ossetian Interior Ministry. 

On September 1, 2004, terrorists seized School No. 1 in Beslan, North Ossetia, during celebrations marking the first day of the school year. More than 1,000 children, parents and teachers were taken hostage and packed into the school gymnasium, which was rigged with explosives. They were held for three days in extreme heat and denied food and water. 

The siege ended on September 3 amid explosions, fire and a fierce battle inside and around the school. 334 people were killed, including 186 children. Hundreds more were wounded. It remains the deadliest school terrorist attack in modern Russian history. 

The gymnasium has been preserved as a memorial, where photographs of the victims, flowers, candles and an Orthodox cross now stand. Every September 1–3, Beslan remembers the three days of the siege.

Named after a 19th-century explorer, the Perito Moreno Glacier is a stunning 19-mile-long ice formation, rising approximately 240 feet above the surface of Lake Argentino. Covering around 121 square miles, it forms part of a vast ice field shared by Argentina and Chile and holds the distinction of being the world’s third-largest reserve of fresh water.

In 1981, it was designated a UNESCO World Heritage site. Today, viewing platforms provide spectacular vantage points where you can watch the glacier calve massive slabs of ice into the turquoise waters—sometimes feeling the chill of its breath on your face.

You can observe these dramatic collapses from shore, take a 45-minute boat tour for a closer look, or even walk across the glacier itself during trekking excursions available from December to March.
